Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

AREA 1. FROZEN RIVER VALLEY
A frozen river valley.
Features: the ice shelf, the cut bank, the driftwood pile, the travois, the fire pit, the windbreak stones, the treeline, the dog harnesses.
Occupants: Kya (at the treeline); Torn (at the fire pit); Mira (at the driftwood pile); The Elder (at the travois).

Episode 1 — The Crypt Below

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ Before this: the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ The adventurer says: "Zankaris — the name on this stone isn't a stranger's. It's your brother's."
△ The adventurer finds a way down at the gravestone and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  THE CRYPT BELOW.
△ Cold air. Stone corridors. Old, very old. The air is thick with "The Echo" — a magical residue that repeats the past.

CHARACTERS

ELARA VANCE (Woman, 28) — The Adventurer / "The Anchor." From a modern world (Seattle, software engineer). Fell through a "soft spot" in reality three years ago. She doesn't have "classes" or "levels" — she has *anchors*: objects, memories, ties to her old world that let her resist the world's narrative logic. She carries a cracked smartphone (dead battery, screen spiderwebbed) — her strongest anchor. She wears a patchwork of local leather and her own hoodie. She is tired, sarcastic, deeply homesick, and terrifyingly competent at *not* being the protagonist of a story.

KEL (Non-binary, ageless appearance ~30s) — The "NPC" Who Broke Script. Formerly a generic "Crypt Guardian" template. Elara's presence glitched their dialogue tree three years ago; they gained self-awareness. Now they follow her, pretending to be a companion. They speak in *italics* when the World tries to force a line on them; they speak *normal* when they fight it. They wear rotting guardian armor they've modified with pockets, bandoliers, a satchel of snacks. They are fascinated by Elara's world ("Tell me again about... 'wifi'.").

THE ADVENTURER (Person, late 20s) — The isekai protagonist. No cheat skills, no system window, no divine blessing. Just a backpack full of modern camping gear, a headlamp with dying batteries, and a fading memory of a world with antibiotics and central heating. Formerly: a junior archivist at a metropolitan library. Currently: mapping the "Morrowfield Necropolis" for a scholar who may not exist. Pragmatic to a fault. Talks to the darkness to keep track of her own mind. She remembers her name but refuses to use it—names have power here, and she hasn't decided if this world deserves hers.

THE GRAVESTONE (Object / Entity) — A slab of weathered grey limestone, roughly hewn, inscribed with a name worn smooth by centuries of acid rain. It moved. Not the stone itself—the earth *around* it shifted when she poured the oil. It breathes, almost imperceptibly. The crack beneath it doesn't lead to a coffin. It leads *elsewhere*. It has been waiting for someone to feed it lamp oil. It has been waiting a very long time.

THE THING IN THE WALLS (Presence) — Not a monster. Not a ghost. The architecture *remembers*. The tunnels beneath the Morrowfield are not carved—they are *grown*, like roots or veins. The walls pulse with a slow, hydraulic rhythm. Something circulates in the dark: not blood, not water. *Memory*. Liquid history. The Adventurer's headlamp disturbs it. The darkness here is not empty; it is *pregnant*.

Just a backpack full of modern camping gear, a headlamp with dying batteries, and a fading memory of a world with antibiotics and central heating. Formerly: a junior archivist at a metropolitan library. Currently: mapping the "Morrowfield Necropolis" for a scholar who may not exist. Pragmatic to a fault. Talks to the darkness to keep track of her own mind. She remembers her name but refuses to use it—names have power here, and she hasn't decided if this world deserves hers.

THE GRAVESTONE (Object / Entity) — A slab of weathered grey limestone, roughly hewn, inscribed with a name worn smooth by centuries of acid rain. It moved. Not the stone itself—the earth *around* it shifted when she poured the oil. It breathes, almost imperceptibly. The crack beneath it doesn't lead to a coffin. It leads *elsewhere*. It has been waiting for someone to feed it lamp oil. It has been waiting a very long time.

THE THING IN THE WALLS (Presence) — Not a monster. Not a ghost. The architecture *remembers*. The tunnels beneath the Morrowfield are not carved—they are *grown*, like roots or veins. The walls pulse with a slow, hydraulic rhythm. Something circulates in the dark: not blood, not water. *Memory*. Liquid history. The Adventurer's headlamp disturbs it. The darkness here is not empty; it is *pregnant*.

CHARACTERS: The Adventurer, The Gravestone (Entity), The Thing in the Walls (Presence)

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system

△ Vellichor, Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy, outside the crypt.

CHARACTERS

△ Now: INT.  CRYPT.
△ Zankaris, a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little, in a crypt under the gravestone.
△ Vellichor, Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy, outside the crypt.

A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Desert world.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: High fantasy isekai.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — Under the Gravestone

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ Before this: the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ The adventurer pours lamp oil into the crack under the gravestone and drops a lit match after it.
△ The adventurer finds a way down at the gravestone and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  UNDER THE GRAVESTONE.
△

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.

△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system

<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: High fantasy isekai.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — Tomb Below

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ Before this: the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ The adventurer pours lamp oil into the crack under the gravestone and drops a lit match after it.
△ The adventurer finds a way down at the gravestone and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  TOMB BELOW.
△ Zankaris enters a tomb. It's a garden of strange flowers, subterranean, lit by soft bioluminescence. Peaceful.
△ Vellichor follows, head low. They walk through the garden.

CHARACTERS

ZANKARIS — a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little

VELLICHOR — Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

Episode 1 — Field of Morrows

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world

CHARACTERS

ZANKARIS — a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little

VELLICHOR — Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.

1.  EXT.  FIELD OF MORROWS

CHARACTERS: Zankaris, Vellichor

△ the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ Zankaris, a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little, in front of the gravestone.

A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Desert world.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

AREA 1. EDGE CAMP
A camp at the crater's rim.

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

AREA 1. FROZEN RIVER VALLEY
A frozen river valley.
Features: the ice shelf, the cut bank, the driftwood pile, the travois, the fire pit, the windbreak stones, the treeline, the dog harnesses.
Occupants: Kya (at the treeline); Torn (at the fire pit); Mira (at the driftwood pile); The Elder (at the travois).

△ Now: INT.  TOMB.
△ A damp, narrow tomb corridor. Stone walls weep moisture.
△ The adventurer moves deeper into the tomb.

CHARACTERS

ZANKARIS — a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little

VELLICHOR — Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy

IRIDA — a wandering scholar (nonhuman), 5: light body, wings that aren't for flying, moth-antennae, luminous skin; deep lore knowledge but zero survival instincts; talks constantly

NERO — a small shadow-familiar, shapeshifter (nonhuman), <1: inky, shifting mass; loyal to Irida; eats magic; communicates through impressions and shapes

THE GRAVEWALKER — a hulking construct of bone and rusted plate: guardian of the tomb's upper levels; no face, only a grille

△ Also:
△ Zankaris's class: PALADIN (Oath of the Morning Star) — [FALLEN]

A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.

1. INT.  TOMB

△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Desert world.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

<|im_start|>system

THE TOMB (Location / Character) — A semi-sentient dungeon. It *remembers* every adventurer who entered. It rearranges itself based on their regrets. It does not want to kill; it wants to *resolve*. CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

THE THING IN THE WALLS (Unknown) — Not a monster. Not a trap. Something *architectural*. The dungeon *is* its body. It breathes through the ventilation shafts. Its heartbeat is the dripping water. It learns *from* Eolh — sarcasm, hesitation, the concept of "mercy" — and finds these variables... inefficient. It resides in the Lens eye.

THE TOMB (Location / Character) — A semi-sentient dungeon. It *remembers* every adventurer who entered. It rearranges itself based on their regrets. It does not want to kill; it wants to *resolve*. Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ Before this: the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ The adventurer leaves by the north mist and keeps going.
△ Now: EXT.  TWISTING WOOD  DAY.
△ Zankaris enters the Twisting Wood. The trees are tall and the path is narrow.
△ Vellichor walks beside her, unbothered.

CHARACTERS

ZANKARIS — a knight of the Church of Morning Star, 21: once the chosen hero, her legend ended in failure; scarred armor, notched sword; she speaks little

VELLICHOR — Zankaris's unicorn: ancient, sentient and sarcastic; he never speaks, not even by telepathy

Episode 1 — The Ledge

△ Space opera.
△ On a space station orbiting a dying star. A character named Merelai is sitting at a window, looking out at the star.
△ A woman named Halkric walks up to her.

CHARACTERS

MERELAI (Woman, 30s) — Former naval strategist, now a recluse. She watches the star die because she orchestrated the operation that killed it. She carries the weight of a billion deaths she ordered to win a war that ended three years ago. She drinks synthetic coffee. She doesn't sleep well.

HALKRIC (Woman, 40s) — Merelai's former XO. Pragmatic, grounded, the only one Merelai still answers comms from. She didn't follow Merelai into retirement; she stayed in the fleet. She's here on official business, but also because she's worried.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

When the "Chosen One" (their childhood friend, Kaelen) arrived from another world, Tayis became the strategist, the quartermaster, the one who calculated the survival odds. When Kaelen died defeating the Dark Lord, the portal home opened. Everyone else went through. Tayis stayed. They swore an oath to tend the graves of the fallen—companions, enemies, the unnamed dead. CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Desert world.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Rotwell

△ Desert world.
△ In the center of the Rotwell, a massive crater filled with strange, mutated life. The Rotwell is a place of danger and opportunity.
△ A small camp sits at the edge of the Rotwell.

CHARACTERS

KAEL (Man, 34) — A "Rotwalker." Someone who enters the Rotwell to harvest valuable materials: crystals, glands, exotic matter. He knows the safe paths, the tidal patterns of the mutation. He’s seen too many friends die. He drinks water like it’s whiskey. He has a mechanical left leg, damaged from a "surge" event years ago.

MIRA (Woman, 28) — Kael’s handler / quartermaster / only friend who stays topside. She runs the camp: supplies, comms, buyers, medical. She monitors Kael’s vitals and the Rotwell’s seismic/mutation readings. She’s sharp, organized, terrified of the day he doesn't come back. She has a prosthetic right eye that links to the camp’s sensor array.

OLD JORAN (Man, 60s) — The only other permanent resident. A former Rotwalker who "retired" (got too mutated to go deep). He maintains the winches, the air scrubbers, the heavy gear. He’s half-crystallized himself — skin like geode on his left side. He mutters to the Rotwell like it’s a neighbor.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  THE ROTWELL — EDGE CAMP  DAY  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kael, Mira, Old Joran

△ The camp at the edge of the Rotwell. Kael is gearing up for a descent. Mira is monitoring. Old Joran is maintaining the winch.
△ A stranger (woman, early 30s) approaches the camp from the wasteland.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting tale. Use beats and directions liberally.
<|im_end|>

1.  FROZEN RIVER VALLEY  DUSK  EXT.

CHARACTERS: Kya, Torn, Mira, The Elder

△ The band arrives at a sheltered bend in the frozen river. Wind howls.
△ They begin to make camp. Urgency.
△ The Elder speaks of a dream.

<|im_start|>system
A strange and interesting set of characters. Script character bios (人物小传).
Genre: High fantasy isekai.
<|im_end|>

Episode 1 — Forgotten Crypt

△ High fantasy isekai.
△ Before this: the field of morrows, an open misty meadow of old graves in a high-fantasy world.
△ The adventurer pours lamp oil into the crack under the gravestone and drops a lit match after it.
△ The adventurer finds a way down at the gravestone and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  FORGOTTEN CRYPT.
△ Zankaris and Vellichor climb down into the forgotten crypt under the gravestone.
△ They explore the dusty, ancient, hollow and dark crypt.

CHARACTERS

Episode 1 — The Drip

△ Swamp country.
△ A small research station in the wetlands.
△ A trio of workers live here: Mallow, Mallow’s son, and Mallow’s employee.

CHARACTERS

MALLOW (Woman, 50s) — The station lead. Practical, weathered, runs a tight ship. She knows the swamp better than the back of her hand. She’s seen too many researchers come and go. She drinks swamp-tea and smokes hand-rolled cigarettes.

MALLOW’S SON — NIM (Man, early 20s) — Born and raised in the swamp. Lanky, quiet, observant. He doesn’t speak much. He maintains the station’s systems — generators, water filtration, comms. He knows every sound of the wetland. He’s never left.

MALLOW’S EMPLOYEE — TEK (Woman, late 20s) — An outsider. Hired for her expertise in anomalous flora. She’s sharp, skeptical, and writes everything down in a waterproof notebook. She’s here for the grant money, but the swamp is getting under her skin. She and Nim have a quiet, unspoken rapport.

HALKRIC (Woman, 40s) — Merelai's former XO. Pragmatic, grounded, the only one Merelai still answers comms from. She didn't follow Merelai into retirement; she stayed in the fleet. She's here on official business, but also because she's worried.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

Episode 1 — The Long Winter

△ Prehistoric world, the last ice age.
△ A small band of humans, the "River People," travel along a frozen river.
△ They stop to make camp for the night.

CHARACTERS

KYA (Woman, 32) — The band’s lead hunter. Broad-shouldered, scarred, pragmatic. She carries a spear tipped with a mammoth ivory point. She speaks rarely, preferring hand signs. She lost her mate two winters past; she does not speak of him. She watches the treeline constantly.

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

<|im_start|>system

TORN (Man, 28) — The band’s toolmaker and fire-keeper. Fingers stained with ochre and resin. He carries the "Fire Horn" — a hollowed bison horn holding a smoldering coal, the band’s most precious possession. He is anxious, inventive, talks to himself when he works. He fears the dark more than the cold.

MIRA (Girl, 12) — Kya’s niece. Torn’s daughter. Quick, quiet, observant. She is learning the hunt but is not yet allowed a spear. She collects small things: feathers, strange stones, beads of amber. She dreams of the "Green Land" the elders speak of in stories.

THE ELDER (Agender, 60+) — The band’s memory. Blind, wrapped in furs. Carries a staff carved with the history of the band. They do not walk; they are carried on a travois pulled by the band’s two surviving dogs. They speak in riddles and old tongues.

Your sprite must look like the same artist drew it.\n\n# House style (measured)\n# Fixion colour-skin house style, v3 (forge3; measured on the shipped sprites)\n\nMeasured with `lib/pixstats3.py` on the 167 shipped tile sprites + 100 authored inn/village sprites (on-style), vs\nround 2's 112 forged candidates (blind judge flagged 49% as \"a different artist\"):\n\n| per prop sprite | shipped median | round-2 forged median |\n|---|---|---|\n| distinct colours (16 levels/channel) | 7.5 | 64 |\n| mean error after reducing to 8 colours | 0.05 | 11.3 |\n| pixels on a smooth gradient ramp | 0% | 16% |\n| edge (detail) pixels | 7% | 15% |\n\nSo the house style is: **a few flat colours, no gradients, no dark outlines, little detail.**\n\n## Format and camera\n- One PNG per map cell, 96x96 RGBA (48 css px at 2x). Multi-cell props are drawn whole and cut into cells.\n- Props: transparent background, the look's floor is drawn under them. Floors, walls, terrain: opaque, seamless.\n- Top-down with a slight 3/4 tilt: an object's top face plus a thin, darker strip of its front. No perspective.\n\n## Shape and colour rules (hard)\n- **Flat fills only.** Each part of an object is ONE colour, at most 2-3 tones per part (top face / front strip /\n  one accent). No gradients, no shading ramps, no stacked concentric highlights, no gloss.\n- **No outlines.** Shapes are separated by tone, never by a dark rim. Do not draw borders around shapes.\n- **Colour budget: 4-7 colours for the whole sprite** (the kit snaps to your 8 most-used fills anyway; colours used\n  for tiny details are lost). Use the look's palette `s.P` and `shade()/lift()` of it; saturated colours only for\n  light, fire, screens.\n- **Detail budget:** one clear silhouette that reads at 48 px + at most 2-3 interior details (a seam, a handle, a\n  slot). Big simple shapes; nothing thinner than 2 px; no texture noise, no scattered tiny dots on props.\n- The silhouette should fill a good part of the cell (props typically cover 25-75% of their cells).\n- Light sources may use `s.glow()` (it spills on the floor behind the object).\n\n## Floors (look tiles)\n- Opaque, seamless (use `tile=True`), **low contrast**: shipped floors have luminance std 2-25, 2-4 colours: one\n  ground colour + 1-2 close tones for boards/cracks/pebbles. Dark-to-mid values (the skin lays light and tints on top).\n- 4 variants that differ only slightly (a crack, a pebble cluster, a board seam offset) so the floor does not repeat.\n\n## Walls (look tiles)\n- Opaque, floorless, made with the `s.wall_part(vp, hp, face)` primitive: a dark cap band on top, the face, a darker\n  base band; side walls / corners get a vertical cap beam. Draw the material (stones, planks, panels, ice blocks,\n  hull plates) flat inside the returned `face` rect, 2 tones. Walls are darker than the floor's props.\n\n## Palettes\n- Existing looks: bar (neon cyber-bar at night: navy-slate, warm wood, pink/cyan neon accents), house (midnight\n  flat: navy wallpaper, walnut, pale linens, brass), boutique (cream marble, dark walnut, gold trim), field (misty\n  night meadow: dark green grass, earth, grey stone), inn (warm wood, beige plaster, dark timber), village (night\n  cobbles, thatch, timber).\n- New looks: a palette dict with the standard keys (floor, wall, wood, wood_light, wood_dark, dark, slate, metal,\n  metal_dark, metal_light, stone, stone_dark, red, green, brass, cloth, accent, accent2, violet, light, paper, water,\n  fire) plus up to 6 look-specific keys. Muted, mid-dark values; one or two accent colours.\n\n# The drawing kit (already in scope: everything from spritekit, plus math and random)\nspritekit3: the FLAT house-style kit for forge3 (round 3). Same API as round 2's spritekit, but the style is\nenforced by the kit itself, because round 2's forged sprites were off-style for measurable pixel reasons\n(exp/forge3: ~64 distinct colours vs ~8 for shipped props, smooth ramps on 16% of pixels vs 0%, dark rims):\n  * no outlines: `edge=` is accepted for compatibility and IGNORED;\n  * flat fills: finish() snaps every opaque pixel to the nearest colour you actually filled with (alpha keeps the\n    smooth silhouette), so gradients, antialias mush and grain cannot appear; no grain;\n  * glows are drawn BEHIND the object (light spill on the floor), never over its fills;\n  * a colour budget: finish() keeps at most `max_colors` (default 8) of your fill colours (the most used ones).\n\nAll coordinates are in 1x sprite pixels: one map cell = 96x96 (48 css px at 2x).\n\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look)          # w, h in cells; s.W = 96*w, s.H = 96*h; s.P = the look's palette (dict of RGB)\n    s.box(x0, y0, x1, y1, fill, r=0)                       # (rounded) rectangle\n    s.ellipse(x0, y0, x1, y1, fill)    s.circle(cx, cy, r, fill)    s.poly([(x, y), ...], fill)\n    s.line([(x, y), ...], color, w=2)  s.arc(x0, y0, x1, y1, start, end, color, w=2)  s.pie(x0, y0, x1, y1, a0, a1, fill)\n    s.block(x0, y0, x1, y1, top, front=14, r=6)            # 3/4 object: top face + darker front strip (2 tones)\n    s.planks(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, across=True, n=4)       # boards: one fill + seam lines (2 tones)\n    s.stones(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, rows=3)                 # blocks in 2 alternating tones on a mortar tone\n    s.metal(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, r=4)                     # slab + one lighter top band (2 tones)\n    s.rivets([(x, y), ...], base)      s.slats(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, n=5, vertical=False)\n    s.glass(x0, y0, x1, y1, tint=None)                     # pane + one gleam line\n    s.flame(cx, cy, size)              s.glow(cx, cy, r, color, alpha=140)   # glow = light spill behind the object\n    s.leaves(cx, cy, r, color=None, n=7)                   # leafy clump in 2 tones\n    s.ripples(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, n=6)   s.speckle(x0, y0, x1, y1, colors, n=40, size=(1, 3))\n    s.screen(x0, y0, x1, y1, color)                        # flat lit display + glow behind\n    s.wall_part(vp, hp, face, cap=None, base=None)         # house primitive for wall tiles (see style_guide3.md):\n        # returns dict(face=(x0,y0,x1,y1), cap=[rects], base=[rects]) after painting them flat; draw the material\n        # (stones / planks / panels) inside 'face' afterwards. vp = t|m|b|s, hp = l|m|r|s (same-kind neighbours).\n    img = s.finish(shadow='auto', max_colors=8)            # -> PIL RGBA image (W x H)\n  Tiles (floors, terrain; opaque, seamless): s = Sprite(1, 1, look, tile=True, ground=COLOR); every shape wraps\n  around the edges; finish() adds no shadow.\n  Colours: RGB tuples. shade(c, f) multiplies (f<1 darker), lift(c, d) adds, mix(a, b, t).\n  s.rnd is a seeded random.Random (use it, never the global random).\n\n# Rules\nOnly the kit + math/random (no imports of anything else, no files, no network). Use s.rnd for randomness. Use the look's palette s.P (and shade/lift/mix of it). Flat fills, 2-3 tones per part, 4-7 colours in total, no outlines, no gradients or stacked highlight rings, at most 2-3 small details, nothing thinner than 2 px, no noise texture on props. Under ~60 lines. Reply with ONE python code block and no prose.\n\n# Examples\n```python\nFOOTPRINT = '1x1'\nSOLID = True\nFLOORLESS = False\n\n\ndef draw(w, h, look, seed):\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look, seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    s.block(18, 22, 78, 84, P['wood'], front=18, r=6)        # top face + front strip: 2 tones\n    s.box(30, 70, 66, 74, P['wood_dark'], r=2)                # one drawer seam\n    s.box(44, 71, 52, 74, P['brass'], r=1)                    # one accent: the handle\n    s.circle(48, 38, 9, P['paper'])                           # a round lamp base on top\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\nFOOTPRINT = 'run_h'\nSOLID = True\nFLOORLESS = False\n\n\ndef draw(w, h, look, seed):\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look, seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    x0, x1 = (10, s.W - 10) if w == 1 else (10, s.W - 10)\n    s.block(x0, 18, x1, 86, P['wood_light'], front=22, r=5)  # one long slab: top + front, no outline\n    for i in range(w):                                        # one seam per cell so the run repeats evenly\n        cx = 96 * i + 48\n        s.box(cx - 14, 34, cx + 14, 46, P['dark'], r=3)      # a sunk tray on each cell's top\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\n# a look's floor tile (called as draw_floor(seed) for 4 variants)\ndef draw_floor(seed):\n    s = Sprite(1, 1, LOOK, tile=True, ground=PALETTE['floor'], seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    s.planks(0, 0, 96, 96, P['floor'], across=True, n=4)      # base + seams: 2 tones, low contrast\n    for _ in range(1 + seed % 2):                              # a slight difference per variant\n        x, y = s.rnd.uniform(0, 80), s.rnd.choice([10, 34, 58, 82])\n        s.box(x, y, x + 16, y + 3, lift(P['floor'], 6), r=1)\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\n# a look's wall part (called as draw_wall(vp, hp, seed) for all 16 neighbour cases)\ndef draw_wall(vp, hp, seed):\n    s = Sprite(1, 1, LOOK, tile=True, ground=PALETTE['wall'], seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    r = s.wall_part(vp, hp, P['wall'], cap=P['dark'], base=shade(P['wall'], 0.75))\n    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r['face']\n    s.stones(x0, y0, x1, y1, P['wall'], rows=3)                # material, flat, 2 tones\n    return s.finish()\n```",

Your sprite must look like the same artist drew it.\n\n# House style (measured)\n# Fixion colour-skin house style, v3 (forge3; measured on the shipped sprites)\n\nMeasured with `lib/pixstats3.py` on the 167 shipped tile sprites + 100 authored inn/village sprites (on-style), vs\nround 2's 112 forged candidates (blind judge flagged 49% as \"a different artist\"):\n\n| per prop sprite | shipped median | round-2 forged median |\n|---|---|---|\n| distinct colours (16 levels/channel) | 7.5 | 64 |\n| mean error after reducing to 8 colours | 0.05 | 11.3 |\n| pixels on a smooth gradient ramp | 0% | 16% |\n| edge (detail) pixels | 7% | 15% |\n\nSo the house style is: **a few flat colours, no gradients, no dark outlines, little detail.**\n\n## Format and camera\n- One PNG per map cell, 96x96 RGBA (48 css px at 2x). Multi-cell props are drawn whole and cut into cells.\n- Props: transparent background, the look's floor is drawn under them. Floors, walls, terrain: opaque, seamless.\n- Top-down with a slight 3/4 tilt: an object's top face plus a thin, darker strip of its front. No perspective.\n\n## Shape and colour rules (hard)\n- **Flat fills only.** Each part of an object is ONE colour, at most 2-3 tones per part (top face / front strip /\n  one accent). No gradients, no shading ramps, no stacked concentric highlights, no gloss.\n- **No outlines.** Shapes are separated by tone, never by a dark rim. Do not draw borders around shapes.\n- **Colour budget: 4-7 colours for the whole sprite** (the kit snaps to your 8 most-used fills anyway; colours used\n  for tiny details are lost). Use the look's palette `s.P` and `shade()/lift()` of it; saturated colours only for\n  light, fire, screens.\n- **Detail budget:** one clear silhouette that reads at 48 px + at most 2-3 interior details (a seam, a handle, a\n  slot). Big simple shapes; nothing thinner than 2 px; no texture noise, no scattered tiny dots on props.\n- The silhouette should fill a good part of the cell (props typically cover 25-75% of their cells).\n- Light sources may use `s.glow()` (it spills on the floor behind the object).\n\n## Floors (look tiles)\n- Opaque, seamless (use `tile=True`), **low contrast**: shipped floors have luminance std 2-25, 2-4 colours: one\n  ground colour + 1-2 close tones for boards/cracks/pebbles. Dark-to-mid values (the skin lays light and tints on top).\n- 4 variants that differ only slightly (a crack, a pebble cluster, a board seam offset) so the floor does not repeat.\n\n## Walls (look tiles)\n- Opaque, floorless, made with the `s.wall_part(vp, hp, face)` primitive: a dark cap band on top, the face, a darker\n  base band; side walls / corners get a vertical cap beam. Draw the material (stones, planks, panels, ice blocks,\n  hull plates) flat inside the returned `face` rect, 2 tones. Walls are darker than the floor's props.\n\n## Palettes\n- Existing looks: bar (neon cyber-bar at night: navy-slate, warm wood, pink/cyan neon accents), house (midnight\n  flat: navy wallpaper, walnut, pale linens, brass), boutique (cream marble, dark walnut, gold trim), field (misty\n  night meadow: dark green grass, earth, grey stone), inn (warm wood, beige plaster, dark timber), village (night\n  cobbles, thatch, timber).\n- New looks: a palette dict with the standard keys (floor, wall, wood, wood_light, wood_dark, dark, slate, metal,\n  metal_dark, metal_light, stone, stone_dark, red, green, brass, cloth, accent, accent2, violet, light, paper, water,\n  fire) plus up to 6 look-specific keys. Muted, mid-dark values; one or two accent colours.\n\n# The drawing kit (already in scope: everything from spritekit, plus math and random)\nspritekit3: the FLAT house-style kit for forge3 (round 3). Same API as round 2's spritekit, but the style is\nenforced by the kit itself, because round 2's forged sprites were off-style for measurable pixel reasons\n(exp/forge3: ~64 distinct colours vs ~8 for shipped props, smooth ramps on 16% of pixels vs 0%, dark rims):\n  * no outlines: `edge=` is accepted for compatibility and IGNORED;\n  * flat fills: finish() snaps every opaque pixel to the nearest colour you actually filled with (alpha keeps the\n    smooth silhouette), so gradients, antialias mush and grain cannot appear; no grain;\n  * glows are drawn BEHIND the object (light spill on the floor), never over its fills;\n  * a colour budget: finish() keeps at most `max_colors` (default 8) of your fill colours (the most used ones).\n\nAll coordinates are in 1x sprite pixels: one map cell = 96x96 (48 css px at 2x).\n\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look)          # w, h in cells; s.W = 96*w, s.H = 96*h; s.P = the look's palette (dict of RGB)\n    s.box(x0, y0, x1, y1, fill, r=0)                       # (rounded) rectangle\n    s.ellipse(x0, y0, x1, y1, fill)    s.circle(cx, cy, r, fill)    s.poly([(x, y), ...], fill)\n    s.line([(x, y), ...], color, w=2)  s.arc(x0, y0, x1, y1, start, end, color, w=2)  s.pie(x0, y0, x1, y1, a0, a1, fill)\n    s.block(x0, y0, x1, y1, top, front=14, r=6)            # 3/4 object: top face + darker front strip (2 tones)\n    s.planks(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, across=True, n=4)       # boards: one fill + seam lines (2 tones)\n    s.stones(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, rows=3)                 # blocks in 2 alternating tones on a mortar tone\n    s.metal(x0, y0, x1, y1, base, r=4)                     # slab + one lighter top band (2 tones)\n    s.rivets([(x, y), ...], base)      s.slats(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, n=5, vertical=False)\n    s.glass(x0, y0, x1, y1, tint=None)                     # pane + one gleam line\n    s.flame(cx, cy, size)              s.glow(cx, cy, r, color, alpha=140)   # glow = light spill behind the object\n    s.leaves(cx, cy, r, color=None, n=7)                   # leafy clump in 2 tones\n    s.ripples(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, n=6)   s.speckle(x0, y0, x1, y1, colors, n=40, size=(1, 3))\n    s.screen(x0, y0, x1, y1, color)                        # flat lit display + glow behind\n    s.wall_part(vp, hp, face, cap=None, base=None)         # house primitive for wall tiles (see style_guide3.md):\n        # returns dict(face=(x0,y0,x1,y1), cap=[rects], base=[rects]) after painting them flat; draw the material\n        # (stones / planks / panels) inside 'face' afterwards. vp = t|m|b|s, hp = l|m|r|s (same-kind neighbours).\n    img = s.finish(shadow='auto', max_colors=8)            # -> PIL RGBA image (W x H)\n  Tiles (floors, terrain; opaque, seamless): s = Sprite(1, 1, look, tile=True, ground=COLOR); every shape wraps\n  around the edges; finish() adds no shadow.\n  Colours: RGB tuples. shade(c, f) multiplies (f<1 darker), lift(c, d) adds, mix(a, b, t).\n  s.rnd is a seeded random.Random (use it, never the global random).\n\n# Rules\nOnly the kit + math/random (no imports of anything else, no files, no network). Use s.rnd for randomness. Use the look's palette s.P (and shade/lift/mix of it). Flat fills, 2-3 tones per part, 4-7 colours in total, no outlines, no gradients or stacked highlight rings, at most 2-3 small details, nothing thinner than 2 px, no noise texture on props. Under ~60 lines. Reply with ONE python code block and no prose.\n\n# Examples\n```python\nFOOTPRINT = '1x1'\nSOLID = True\nFLOORLESS = False\n\n\ndef draw(w, h, look, seed):\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look, seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    s.block(18, 22, 78, 84, P['wood'], front=18, r=6)        # top face + front strip: 2 tones\n    s.box(30, 70, 66, 74, P['wood_dark'], r=2)                # one drawer seam\n    s.box(44, 71, 52, 74, P['brass'], r=1)                    # one accent: the handle\n    s.circle(48, 38, 9, P['paper'])                           # a round lamp base on top\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\nFOOTPRINT = 'run_h'\nSOLID = True\nFLOORLESS = False\n\n\ndef draw(w, h, look, seed):\n    s = Sprite(w, h, look, seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    x0, x1 = (10, s.W - 10) if w == 1 else (10, s.W - 10)\n    s.block(x0, 18, x1, 86, P['wood_light'], front=22, r=5)  # one long slab: top + front, no outline\n    for i in range(w):                                        # one seam per cell so the run repeats evenly\n        cx = 96 * i + 48\n        s.box(cx - 14, 34, cx + 14, 46, P['dark'], r=3)      # a sunk tray on each cell's top\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\n# a look's floor tile (called as draw_floor(seed) for 4 variants)\ndef draw_floor(seed):\n    s = Sprite(1, 1, LOOK, tile=True, ground=PALETTE['floor'], seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    s.planks(0, 0, 96, 96, P['floor'], across=True, n=4)      # base + seams: 2 tones, low contrast\n    for _ in range(1 + seed % 2):                              # a slight difference per variant\n        x, y = s.rnd.uniform(0, 80), s.rnd.choice([10, 34, 58, 82])\n        s.box(x, y, x + 16, y + 3, lift(P['floor'], 6), r=1)\n    return s.finish()\n```\n```python\n# a look's wall part (called as draw_wall(vp, hp, seed) for all 16 neighbour cases)\ndef draw_wall(vp, hp, seed):\n    s = Sprite(1, 1, LOOK, tile=True, ground=PALETTE['wall'], seed=seed)\n    P = s.P\n    r = s.wall_part(vp, hp, P['wall'], cap=P['dark'], base=shade(P['wall'], 0.75))\n    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r['face']\n    s.stones(x0, y0, x1, y1, P['wall'], rows=3)                # material, flat, 2 tones\n    return s.finish()\n```",

opaque, seamless): s = Sprite(1, 1, look, tile=True, ground=COLOR); every shape wraps\n  around the edges; finish() adds no shadow.\n  Colours: RGB tuples. shade(c, f) multiplies (f<1 darker), lift(c, d) adds, mix(a, b, t).\n  s.rnd is a seeded random.Random (use it, never the global random).\n\n# Rules\nOnly the kit + math/random (no imports of anything else, no files, no network).
